chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abd al-Rahman from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who performed voluntary circumambulation (Tawaf) and prayed two rak'ahs while not in a state of ablution (Wudu), he said: 'He must repeat the two rak'ahs but does not need to repeat the circumambulation.'

And whoever interrupts his circumambulation by entering the House (Kaaba) or by going for his own need or for someone else's need: if he has passed half, he builds upon it; and if he has not passed half, and his circumambulation was the obligatory one, he repeats the circumambulation; and if it was the voluntary one, he builds upon it; and if it was less than half, he narrated that (he repeats it).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on repeating Tawaf if interrupted before or after completing half?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between ritual purity (Wudu) and ritual completeness (Tamm) in Tawaf, ruling that minor impurity invalidates the accompanying two Rak'ahs but not the circumambulation itself. It further details the jurisprudence of interruption (Qat'), establishing that voluntary Tawaf is more lenient than obligatory Hajj Tawaf, reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical ease in ritual worship.
